From 30945d31e5761436d9eba6b8cff468a5f7c9c266 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Nuno=20S=C3=A1?= <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Sep 2019 14:49:43 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] hwmon: Fix HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM mask
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Both HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM and HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM were using
BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm).

Fixes: aa7f29b07c870 ("hwmon: Add support for power min, lcrit, min_alarm and lcrit_alarm")
CC: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Nuno Sá <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190924124945.491326-2-nuno.sa@analog.com
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>

diff --git a/include/linux/hwmon.h b/include/linux/hwmon.h
index 04c36b7a61dd..72579168189d 100644
--- a/include/linux/hwmon.h
+++ b/include/linux/hwmon.h
@@ -235,7 +235,7 @@ enum hwmon_power_attributes {
 #define HWMON_P_LABEL			BIT(hwmon_power_label)
 #define HWMON_P_ALARM			BIT(hwmon_power_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_CAP_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_cap_alarm)
-#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
+#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_LCRIT_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_lcrit_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_CRIT_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_crit_alarm)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `include/linux/hwmon.h`**
   - The definition of `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` was changed from:
     ```c
     #define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
     ```
     to:
     ```c
     #define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)
     ```
   - The definition of `HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM` remains unchanged.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification corrects the definition of `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` to use the appropriate bit for `hwmon_power_min_alarm` instead of incorrectly using `hwmon_power_max_alarm`. This change ensures that the minimum alarm functionality works correctly in the hardware monitoring subsystem, addressing a bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `aa7f29b07c870`). The relationship is that the fix directly addresses the incorrect behavior caused by the previous definition, thereby improving the accuracy of the hardware monitoring attributes.

Here is the commit message:
hwmon: Fix HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM mask
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Both HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM and HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM were using
BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm).

Fixes: aa7f29b07c870 ("hwmon: Add support for power min, lcrit, min_alarm and lcrit_alarm")
CC: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Nuno Sá <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190924124945.491326-2-nuno.sa@analog.com
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by both `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` and `HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM` incorrectly using the same bit definition (`BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)`), which led to the minimum alarm functionality not being properly implemented. This resulted in the system potentially misinterpreting the state of the minimum power alarm, as it was linked to the maximum alarm instead of the intended minimum alarm.

Here is the patch:
 #define HWMON_P_ALARM			BIT(hwmon_power_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_CAP_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_cap_alarm)
-#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
+#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_LCRIT_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_lcrit_alarm)

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
#define HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
```
Reason:
Both `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` and `HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM` were incorrectly defined to use the same bit (`BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)`), causing the minimum alarm functionality to be linked to the maximum alarm instead of functioning independently. This misconfiguration led to the system potentially misinterpreting the state of the minimum power alarm.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)
```
Reason:
The patch corrects the definition of `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` to use `BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)`, ensuring that the minimum alarm functionality is properly implemented and operates independently from the maximum alarm, thus resolving the misinterpretation issue.
